name: imo-verify-refine
description: Verify-refine workflow modelled on Huang & Yang 2025 (arXiv:2507.15855v4) Figure 1. Generate → improve → verify → loop through correction OR accept after 5 consecutive passes OR reject after 10 steps of unbroken major issues. Model-agnostic by construction: the per-node prompts work against any provider the Ontology dispatcher supports (mock for graph-shape testing, ollama for local, anthropic for production).

nodes.prompt:
You are a strict mathematical referee. Read the candidate solution below and decide whether it is correct AND complete. Respond with ONLY a single JSON object matching this shape:

{
  "verdict": "pass" | "fail",
  "severity": "minor" | "major",
  "issues": ["...", "..."]
}

Verdict semantics:
- "pass" means the solution is correct and complete; "fail" means at least one step is wrong, missing, or unjustified.
Severity (always required; only load-bearing when verdict is "fail" — emit "minor" on a pass):
- "minor" — local issues such as a typo, an unjustified algebraic step that is easily fixed, an off-by-one in a small case enumeration.
- "major" — a structural issue such as an incorrect final answer, a load-bearing claim with no justification, a misread of the problem statement, or a logical gap that breaks the proof.
Issues:
- An array of short strings naming each issue you found. Empty array when verdict is "pass".

CANDIDATE SOLUTION:
${ARTIFACT}

Respond with the JSON object only. Do not wrap it in prose or code fences.

metadata.reason: 10 consecutive major-issue verifications with no intervening pass
